question: Each person who shares a post leads on average to 0.8 more sharers. Starting from one share, how many shares in total, eventually?
answer: About 5 shares in all: below one onward sharer each, a cascade fizzles fast.
move: Below one onward copy each, nothing spreads far, however good it is.
ask: When I hope something I made will spread, do I know how many people each viewer passes it to?
trap: 0.8 is close to 1, so the post should still spread widely.
hint: Add the first share, the 0.8 it causes, the 0.64 those cause, and so on.
steps: A chain shrinking by 0.8 each step sums to 1 ÷ (1 − 0.8)
About 5 shares in all: below one onward sharer each, a cascade fizzles fast.
reference: Adam Kucharski, The Rules of Contagion: Why Things Spread, and Why They Stop, Profile Books, 2020
